sections.h2: Where is the Town of Babylon, and which communities does it cover?
sections.html:
The Town of Babylon is one of ten towns in Suffolk County, on the south shore of Long Island. It borders Nassau County to the west, Huntington to the north, Islip to the east and the Atlantic Ocean to the south. At its western edge it is about 20 miles from the Queens line.

The town holds three incorporated villages and a long list of hamlets, so the name on a mailing address often means a different set of rules from the name of the town.

  • Villages: Amityville in the southwest, Lindenhurst in the south and Babylon in the southeast
  • Hamlets: Copiague, Deer Park, East Farmingdale, North Amityville, North Babylon, North Lindenhurst, West Babylon, Wheatley Heights and Wyandanch
  • Barrier-island communities: Gilgo, Oak Beach, Captree and part of Fire Island west of the Robert Moses Causeway

Town Hall is on East Sunrise Highway in Lindenhurst. If your house sits inside one of the three villages, ask whether the village adds its own taxes or permits on top of the town's.

sections.h2: How did Babylon grow from a bay settlement into a town of 219,766 people?
sections.html:
Babylon was once called Huntington South. Two families moved there and gave it the name New Babylon around 1803, and the town was formed in 1872 by splitting it off from the Town of Huntington.

Growth came fast after the war. The census counted 45,556 residents in 1950 and 142,309 in 1960, then 204,256 in 1970. The population has held near 200,000 or more ever since and reached 218,223 in 2020. Houses built in that stretch are now decades old, and buyers expect to see the age of the roof and heating system.

A population that big fills a lot of housing, and the town's three villages and many hamlets each have their own character. Buyers compare streets closely, so know which hamlet or village your address falls in.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Babylon?
sections.html:
Babylon is a homeowner town with high costs. About 78.3% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $522,100, with typical owner costs of $3,206 a month for those who carry a mortgage.

sections.h2: How do Babylon's trains, airports and roads affect buyers?
sections.html:
The Long Island Rail Road's Babylon Branch is the main rail line, running from the Nassau County line to the Village of Babylon with stops from Amityville to Babylon. The Main Line crosses the north of town with stations at Pinelawn, Wyandanch and Deer Park. Suffolk County Transit buses fill in the rest.

Republic Airport in East Farmingdale houses the American Airpower Museum, and Long Island MacArthur Airport in Ronkonkoma, nearby, has commercial flights. The mean commute for Babylon workers is 31.0 minutes, against 26.4 for the country.

For sellers, distance to a station is a headline feature. Put the station name in your listing or your cash-buyer conversation, because walkable-to-train houses draw a different pool of buyers than houses a long drive from one.

sections.h2: What does living near the Great South Bay mean for a Babylon house?
sections.html:
More than half of the town's 114 square miles is water. The town sits at an elevation of about 6.6 feet, with the Great South Bay, Fire Island Inlet and Atlantic beaches along its southern line. Town parks include Southard's Pond Park in the village and Tanner Park in Copiague, and state parks include Belmont Lake, Captree and Robert Moses.

Low ground and open water shape insurance, repairs and buyer questions. Ask your insurance agent whether your house sits in a flood zone before you list.

Sewer billing changed this year. Effective January 1, 2026, all Suffolk County sewer districts merged into the Suffolk County Wastewater Management District, and the rate or billing method for your property may be different. Look at the sewer line on your tax bill.

sections.h2: When are Babylon property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
The Babylon tax year runs from December 1 to November 30, and bills are mailed once a year around mid-December. You can pay in full or in two halves. For the 2025-26 year, the first half was due in the second week of January 2026 and the second half at the end of May, and both dates have passed. The 2026-27 bill is expected in mid-December.

  • Late first-half payments add 1% per month, reaching 5% for payments in mid to late May.
  • After the last May payment date, taxes become delinquent and are paid to the Suffolk County Comptroller in Riverhead, with a 5% penalty plus 1% interest per month counted from February 1.
  • Partial payments of $200 or more are accepted.
  • Online card payments carry a 2.35% fee, and e-checks cost $1.
  • If taxes stay unpaid until the tax lien sale, usually in December, Suffolk County sells a lien on the property.

The Receiver of Taxes does not set rates. School budgets, the county and the town set the amounts, and school tax is usually the largest line. Not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and assessment challenges work in Babylon?
sections.html:
Exemption applications in the Town of Babylon are due by March 1, and late ones are denied. The town administers Enhanced STAR, Aged, Alternative Veterans, Cold War Veterans, volunteer firefighter and ambulance worker, disability with limited income, Capital Improvement and first-time buyer on newly built homes. New Basic STAR applicants receive a credit from New York State instead of a school tax exemption.

A key point for sellers: exemptions belong to the person who qualified. A buyer of a house with a senior or veteran exemption should expect the exemption to drop off, which can raise the tax bill sharply. Warn your buyer about it up front.

Assessment challenges use Form RP-524. In Suffolk County, the town Board of Assessment Review meets on the third Tuesday in May, which falls on May 18 in 2027. The Babylon Department of Assessment builds values from square footage and amenities and posts exemption forms on its pages.

sections.h2: What does closing a Babylon sale involve, and how does a cash offer fit in?
sections.html:
The seller pays New York's transfer tax of $2 for each $500 of price. Form TP-584 is filed with the Suffolk County Clerk, with payment due within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Third-party payers such as banks, title companies and attorneys pay a $1 duplicate tax bill fee, sent as a separate check. Plan for that when a title company clears your open tax bill at closing.

A listing sale in Babylon runs on the buyer's mortgage timeline. A cash purchase is as-is and can close when you are ready, which suits a house with deferred repairs, a delinquent tax balance or a family estate to settle. Either way, have your deed, the latest tax statement and your lender payoff ready.

faqs.q: When are Babylon property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in mid-December. The first half is due in the second week of January and the second half at the end of May, with penalties rising 1% a month on the first half after the January date.

faqs.q: Who do I pay after May 31 in Babylon?
faqs.a: Taxes paid after May 31 go to the Suffolk County Comptroller's Office in Riverhead. A 5% penalty applies, plus interest of 1% per month counted from February 1.

faqs.q: Will a buyer keep my STAR or senior exemption in Babylon?
faqs.a: No. Exemptions do not pass to a new owner automatically, so a buyer applies on their own and the tax bill may rise. Applications are due March 1.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax on a sale in Babylon?
faqs.a: Yes. New York charges $2 per $500 of price, normally paid by the seller, and Form TP-584 is filed with the Suffolk County Clerk within 15 days of the deed.

faqs.q: What is the grievance deadline in Babylon?
faqs.a: Suffolk County town review boards meet on the third Tuesday in May. Filing is free, uses Form RP-524 and does not require a lawyer.
